messages:
morgan: Quick design review request — pushed a small update to the autoscale panel in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/auto-panel (see frames: pool-swap, burst-fallback, minmax-focus). Main asks: 1) copy for graceful fallback when burst unavailable, 2) confirmation flow for switching GPU pools, 3) keyboard focus & aria states for min/max steppers. Need quick reactions and any accessibility flags. :eyes:
marisol: looked — nice. A couple of quick notes: the fallback copy currently reads 'We switched to lower-capacity pool'. feels too passive. suggest 'Switched to backup pool to preserve latency SLOs'. more proactive.
kevin: agree w/ marisol. also the yellow warning chip feels visually similar to the burst badge. can we differentiate with an icon? maybe a small shield or arrow-down.
eli: on pool-switch confirmation — implementation wise we have 2 async steps (drain connections, remap routing). UX should reflect that it's not instant. propose: Primary CTA 'Switch pool' + secondary 'Switch & wait' ? not sure.
sam: +1 to showing in-progress state. users get nervous when ops take seconds. proposal microcopy: after click show toast 'Switching pools — traffic will move gradually (30–90s).'
marisol: love that. For the confirmation modal copy propose: header 'Confirm pool switch', body: 'Switching this route to GPU pool "Turing-4x" will move new requests to the selected pool. In-flight requests are unaffected. This may change latency and cost.' buttons: 'Cancel' and 'Switch pools'.
kevin: small nit — avoid quoting internal pool names directly in copy unless user owns them; better: include the friendly pool name plus tooltip to show full id. e.g., Turing (turing-4x).
morgan: good call. also we discussed an undo affordance elsewhere — can we add a small snackbar with 'Undo' for 2 minutes? helps rollback accidental swaps.
eli: undo is tricky for routing changes but we can do a programmatic rollback if no persistent state changed. we can implement a 2-min inverse switch that triggers the previous mapping. engineering ok with a snackbar-triggered rollback.
a11y-bot: accessibility note — confirmation modal must trap focus and set aria-live to polite for the status updates. also ensure the toast has role="status" and aria-atomic="true" so screen readers announce switching progress.
marisol: thanks @a11y-bot — will add. Next: burst fallback copy. Current toast: 'Burst unavailable, trying next pool'. feels terse. how about two variants: concise for power users and longer for new users. concise: 'Burst unavailable — using backup capacity.' verbose: 'Requested burst capacity unavailable. We used reserved capacity from Pool B to keep requests within your latency target.'
kevin: verbose is good for first-run, but we need a space-saving one-line in the activity feed. maybe show inline icon for 'fallback' and expand for details on hover/click.
morgan: UX question: do we let users opt-out of fallback (i.e., strict SLO fail instead of using backup pool)? we had a checkbox in early mocks.
sam: business-wise we should default to graceful fallback (keep service up). opt-out should be hidden in advanced settings and require confirmation.
eli: implementation detail: fallback routing can be prioritized by policy (latency-first, cost-first). if we expose opt-out, need to surface the policy consequences. that's product work.
marisol: copy for opt-out confirmation: 'Disable automatic fallback? If you disable, requests may be throttled or produce errors when burst capacity is exhausted.' buttons: 'Keep enabled' and 'Disable fallback'.
a11y-bot: keyboard/accessibility for min/max stepper: ensure stepper controls are real <button> elements, not just icons. Add aria-labels like 'Decrease minimum instances' and 'Increase maximum instances'. also expose aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow on the input region, and implement focus-visible styles.
kevin: front-end note: current stepper is a hidden input with custom divs — changing to real buttons is a small refactor but worth it. screen readers will announce button semantics.
morgan: great — can we standardize the stepper focus ring across the console? current ring looks different in hub vs capacity card.
marisol: yes, I'll update the token for focus outline to use our global focus token (focus-3). should be consistent.
kevin: another keyboard flow: when user tabs into the stepper, arrow keys should increment/decrement values. make sure it's not conflicting with page scroll. implement keydown handlers on the input region.
a11y-bot: add role="spinbutton" to the stepper container and aria-valuetext to describe 'Min instances: 2'. that enables native semantics.
eli: for burst toggle accessibility, ensure we have a visible label and the toggle is reachable via keyboard with space/enter toggling. also the descriptive tooltip should be accessible (focusable help icon).
sam: copy tweak request: on the SLO slider when user drags toward lower latency, callout copy 'Lower latency = higher cost'. maybe show a small cost delta preview next to the knob.
marisol: agreed. in the slider mock I'll add a live preview chip that updates as you drag. it should be aria-live polite so screen readers get the cost change.
a11y-bot: confirm aria-live on that preview and ensure it's not verbose — only announce when value changes due to user action.
morgan: final question — do we want to surface these fallback events in the activity log with expand details (who/when/why)? seems helpful for debugging.
sam: yes, definitely. activity log entry example: '2026-03-12 10:12 — Route X used fallback capacity (Pool B) due to burst limit; policy=latency-first; triggered by autoscale'. include link to the rollout.
marisol: OK I will update Figma with: revised copy for confirmation modal, new toast wording, undo snackbar, explicit opt-out modal copy, focus and aria notes. I'll ping again when done. :white_check_mark:
kevin: I can take the stepper -> buttons refactor and wire up keyboard handlers.
eli: I'll design the rollback API spec and outline events for the activity log.
a11y-bot: accessibility checklist added to the design task: trap focus, role="spinbutton", toast role="status", aria-live for previews, keyboard handlers for toggles.
morgan: thanks everyone — aim to ship copy + a11y tweaks for next sprint. if anyone spots anything else in the Figma drop please add comments there. :rocket:
